title: Address to County Lookup: FIPS and Context
description: Verify an address's county with a Census point-in-polygon lookup using Address to County Lookup — FIPS code, boundary and context. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, an address on Chicago's South Side resolves to Cook County, FIPS 17031 — a code, not just a name, so databases can agree about it.
quick_answer: Address to County Lookup verifies which US county an address, place or point falls in by testing it against Census Bureau county polygons — not by trusting the address's own text. Search the address and read the county name, its FIPS code, the highlighted boundary and Census demographic context.
steps_intro: Addresses lie about counties more often than you would think. Test the point, not the label:

use_cases.title: Forms and filings that need the county

body.t: Tax, legal, licensing and grant forms ask for county and punish guesses. The polygon's answer is the defensible one.
A customer file's county column filled by postal city is wrong at every county line. Verify the important records — bulk thinking continues in the
County-level rules differ across a street. Knowing which side of the line an address sits on is a business fact, delivered here with its FIPS.
The demographic summary that rides along (population, income, home values) makes the county a place with a profile, not just a polygon.
Many addresses carry a mailing city in the neighbouring county. The address text says one county; the point-in-polygon test says the true one — and the FIPS settles arguments.
The White House sits in the District of Columbia — a county-equivalent with FIPS 11001. Independent cities and DC test the tool exactly because they break the usual rules.

faq: Is this just reading the county name from the address?
No — that is exactly what it refuses to do. It geocodes the point and tests which Census county polygon contains it, which is why it catches postal-city mismatches.
Where do the demographic figures come from?
US Census Bureau data (ACS estimates and land-area figures), shown as context with their source. They describe the county, not the household at the address.
Can I search by ZIP code?
Yes — a ZIP or place resolves to a point, and the point is tested. Deep accuracy still wants the full street address.
Is the boundary suitable for a legal survey?
No. Census boundaries are statistical and administrative references, not surveyed legal lines. Property questions need a licensed surveyor.
Why can ACS figures differ from a local source?
Vintage and method: ACS figures are survey estimates over a period; local counts may be newer or counted differently. Both can be honest and disagree.
What about independent cities?
US county-equivalents include independent cities, parishes (Louisiana) and boroughs (Alaska) — the lookup returns the equivalent unit, as the White House example shows.
County or county-equivalent for Puerto Rico?
Municipios are the equivalents there; the Census framework the tool uses treats them as such.
The address sits exactly on a county line.
Lines have width in the real world: buildings straddle, parcels split. The point tested is the address's resolved point — for a straddling property, a surveyor, not a lookup, is the authority.
Can I look up by coordinates alone?
Yes — a point is a point. GPS coordinates or a map click test against the same polygons.
Why does the mailing city disagree with the result?
Postal cities are delivery conveniences that ignore county lines cheerfully. The polygon is the geography; the postmark is the mail's fiction.
Are county populations live counts?
No — Census estimates with a vintage, refreshed on the Census Bureau's cycle. The page labels the source rather than dressing estimates as a census of today.
